answer: An agent economy can pin each identity to a distinct network position the way a glacier pins a landscape: peers scattered across the network send unpredictable latency probes, and an identity must answer each probe from one consistent location, like a juniper rooted in one spot. A single operator running a thousand clones behind one connection cannot fake a thousand different round-trip signatures, so the clones collapse into one pigment smear of identical timing. Each extra identity then needs its own real network presence, and that cost grows with every fake.
